result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Comparison.n_failed]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: The number of test units that failed. twitter-card: title: >- [Comparison.n_failed]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: The number of test units that failed. title: >- [Comparison.n_failed]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The number of test units that failed. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The number of test units that failed. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [Comparison.n_failed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} A test unit fails if its status is `"changed"`, `"missing"`, `"extra"`, or `"dup_key"`. If the schema check failed (see [`schema_ok`](`pointblank.Comparison.schema_ok`)), every test unit fails, so `n_failed` equals [`n`](`pointblank.Comparison.n`). It's always `n - n_passed`. A count of zero failures, along with a passing schema check, is what makes a comparison [`identical`](`pointblank.Comparison.identical`). To see how the failures break down by status, use [`status_counts`](`pointblank.Comparison.status_counts`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} One station's reading changed, one station was dropped, and one was added. ::: {#434ad40c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl readings_v1 = pl.DataFrame( {"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"], "temp": [12.1, 14.0, 9.8, 11.2]} ) readings_v2 = pl.DataFrame( {"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S5"], "temp": [12.1, 14.3, 9.8, 8.0]} ) comparison = pb.compare(readings_v1, readings_v2, keys="station") comparison.n_failed ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A count is useful for a quick check, for instance to stop a script when too many rows differ: ::: {#a60d3236 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} if comparison.n_failed > 0.25 * comparison.n: print(f"{comparison.n_failed} of {comparison.n} rows differ") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 3 of 5 rows differ ``` ::: ::: To act on failures with thresholds and actions instead, compare the tables in a validation with [`Validate.tbl_match()`](`pointblank.Validate.tbl_match`).
